title: Grades 3–5 Mini Test — Listening: The Water Cycle
tier: Classroom practice; not an ACCESS tier
overview: A short listening practice. Listen to a science teacher explain where a puddle went. Then answer six questions. You can listen as many times as you need.

sections.title: Science Talk: Where Did the Puddle Go?
sections.directions: You will hear a teacher or a visitor talk. Press play to listen. You can listen again if you need to. Then answer each question. Choose the best answer.

items.title: The Puddle
items.prompt: What did Mr. Haddad notice this morning?

options.text: The puddle was full of leaves.

items.scriptTitle: Science Talk: Where Did the Puddle Go?
script: Good morning, scientists! Yesterday it rained, and there was a big puddle on the playground. This morning, the puddle is gone. Where did the water go?
The sun warmed the puddle. The heat turned the water into a gas called water vapor. This is called evaporation. The water vapor rose up into the sky.
High in the sky, the air is cold. The cold air turns the water vapor back into tiny drops of water. The drops come together and make clouds. This is called condensation.
When the drops in a cloud get big and heavy, they fall back to the ground as rain or snow. This is called precipitation. Then the water cycle starts all over again!
items.correct: Correct. This morning, the puddle was gone.
items.support: He asks a question about where the water went.

items.title: The Water Cycle
items.prompt: Put the steps of the water cycle in order.

items.text: Drops come together and make clouds.
Rain falls back to the ground.
Water vapor rises into the sky.

items.hint: Mr. Haddad tells the steps in order.
items.support: Start with the puddle and the sun.
